$comment: The code → Figma conversion standard (root CLAUDE.md rule 16). The ONE source of how a code prop becomes a Figma property and how a component's variants are drawn — read by scripts/figma/prop-rule.ts (pnpm docs:figma-map, pnpm figma:props) and scripts/figma/expected-styles.ts. Human-readable twin: .ai/maps/figma-conversion.md. Changing this file is the design-system owner's decision (owner gate). A component needs its own approval only for an exception (contract figma.propertyMap).

naming.property: Figma property name = code prop name, unchanged (isLoading, not loading; children, not label). Every Figma property name is camelCase, like code — never a space (owner's decision 2026-10-21).
naming.values: VARIANT values = code values, unchanged (primary, stacked-bar, false).
naming.optionalText: {name}Text — the TEXT property that holds an optional string's content (descriptionText).
naming.iconSwap: {name}Swap — the INSTANCE_SWAP of an icon prop next to its BOOLEAN {name} (iconSwap): Figma refuses two properties with one name.
naming.layers: Layer names = the data-helix-part values in the TSX, never invented. Visually hidden native inputs (checkbox-input, radio-input, select-native) are not layers.

rules.when: handlers (on*), default* twins, aria-*, ids, refs, data arrays and wiring props
rules.why: behaviour or data, nothing to draw

rules.when: a ReactElement, or ReactNode children of a component that isn't in textChildren
rules.why: another component or free content, not a property
closed = not on screen; Figma draws it open
shows the icon · which icon (Figma refuses two properties with one name, so the swap is {name}Swap — owner's decision 2026-10-20)

rules.when: a list prop (listCount.props) the component hands straight to another Helix component that draws the items — found in the code: <Menu options={options}> in Select and MultiSelect. Checked before list-count
rules.why: the nested component owns the count: the component holds an exposed instance of it (in the open state when it's an overlay) and the designer picks how many items on that instance (owner's rule 2026-10-21)

rules.when: a list of items the component draws one after another — a prop named in listCount.props (options, actions, avatars, items), typed as an array
figma: VARIANT {name} = how many items: listCount.min … listCount.max (2 … 7)
rules.why: Figma can't loop over data: the designer picks how many items the instance shows (owner's rule 2026-10-21)

rules.when: a union of string or number literals
a boolean listed in showHideBooleans — it only shows or hides one part
any other boolean — it changes a color, size or layout (a Figma BOOLEAN can only show/hide a layer)
an optional ReactNode (header, actions, footer, start, end, sidenav, topbar…)
a required string that a part renders, a required ReactNode, placeholder, or children of a textChildren component
an optional string rendered by its own part ({prefix}-{part suffix} in the anatomy, or a *Label prop)

a string — required or optional — that no part renders: no {prefix}-{name} layer in the anatomy (a label can also render as the -legend, -title, -content or -initials part). IconButton's, FAB's, ChipGroup's and SegmentedControl's label, Chart's description
rules.why: read by screen readers only (aria-label) — there is no text to draw (owner's decision 2026-10-20)

why.src: an image URL: Figma can't load an image from a URL, so there is never a src property. The look it decides — photo or initials — is a withImage false/true VARIANT (Avatar, AvatarGroup), approved in the contract's figma.propertyMap / figmaOnly (owner's decision 2026-10-21).
why.aria-*: aria-describedby, aria-label… are read by screen readers only and are set by code (Tooltip sets aria-describedby on its trigger) — nothing to draw, never a Figma property (owner's decision 2026-10-21). Components on a native element accept them without declaring them; only Avatar (a <span>) and Tooltip declare aria-describedby, so it can be a Tooltip trigger.

listCount.owner: The count belongs to the component that draws the items, never to a component that contains it (owner's rule 2026-10-21). AvatarGroup draws its avatars, Menu its options, FAB its actions: each has the count VARIANT. Select and MultiSelect hand their options to Menu (<Menu options={options}>): they have no options property — their state=open variants hold an exposed nested Menu instance (isExposedInstance) and the designer picks the count on it. Detected from the code (rule list-delegated, scripts/figma/prop-rule.ts) and checked by the Figma audit (check 12): a delegating set must hold an exposed instance of the component it delegates to.
listCount.itemsAtRest: Inside a list component's own set (Menu, CheckboxGroup…), every nested item instance is at state=default — hover, press and selected are the item component's own states (MenuItem state=selected), drawn on the item, never inside the list (owner's rule 2026-10-21). Audit check 12.
listCount.rule: Every list of drawn items converts to a VARIANT named like the prop whose values are the item counts (options = 2 / 3 / … / 7) — the Figma property is named exactly like that component's code prop — one variant per count, each item an instance of the item component, with its own example text. The range is 2…7 (owner's decision 2026-10-21) unless the contract's figma.listCount sets { "<prop>": { "min": n, "max": n } } (AvatarGroup's avatars keep 1–7, built before the rule). A list shown only inside an overlay is drawn in the open state. Data that isn't drawn item by item — selected values (value, values, defaultValue), chart categories and series — stays code only (skip).

storyCoverage: Every Storybook story of a component (each export of apps/storybook/stories/{Components,Layout}/{Name}.stories.tsx) says how Figma represents it, or carries the owner's decision that it doesn't (owner's rule 2026-10-21 — Avatar's With image / Initials stories had no Figma counterpart until withImage was added). The contract's figma.stories maps each export: "prop=value, prop=value" (the Figma properties/values that draw it, each a property of the set or state), "default" (the set's default variant), "layout" (a showcase that only arranges existing variants), or { figma: null, reason, approved } (behaviour only, or not drawn on purpose). A keyboard story is a focus state and focus is drawn: it maps to state=focus, or to layout when the ring belongs to a child instance (owner's decision 2026-10-21). pnpm docs:figma-map prints a Stories → Figma block per component (✗ = no approved representation, or a stale entry) and figma-drift fails a component with a ✗. Filling figma.stories is the owner's decision: an agent shows each ✗ story with a proposal and asks.
propertyOrder: Figma properties come in the code's order — the contract's props order, which is the order Storybook's Controls list them in (owner's decision 2026-10-21). Figma always shows VARIANT properties first, so each group follows the code order on its own: the variants in code order with state last, then every other property in code order — a BOOLEAN's {name}Text / {name}Swap right after it, approved exceptions for native attributes last. pnpm docs:figma-map checks it (Property order line) and figma-drift fails a component that breaks it. The reference is the order Storybook's props table really shows, read by pnpm figma:story-order into .ai/storybook-prop-order.json — not the contract's order (Storybook doesn't follow it: Chip's label comes first in Storybook, fourth in the contract). Re-run it whenever a story or a component's props change. Both sides list the same way: Figma can't interleave VARIANT properties with the rest, so Storybook lists the props that are Figma variants first, then the rest (the order of each story file's meta.args sets it) — every group in the same order on both sides (owner's rule 2026-10-21; figma-map's **Storybook order** check).

state.rule: The only Figma-only property: CSS pseudo-classes. disabled, invalid, checked, isLoading… are never values of state — each is its own false/true VARIANT.

variants.disabled: disabled=true is drawn only with state=default and invalid=false — a disabled control doesn't hover, take focus or validate. Every text layer (label, description, required *, legend) binds text/disabled (.ai/maps/patterns/disabled-state.md).
variants.secondary: Secondary look toggles (secondaryAxes) are drawn at every size and in every state the code can reach — fullWidth with default/hover/press/focus and disabled, like any other variant (owner's decision 2026-10-21, replacing 'drawn once'). Except where code makes a state impossible: isLoading disables Button, IconButton and Input (disabled={disabled || isLoading}), so a loading one is drawn at state=default only, enabled and valid. hideLabel is drawn in every state too.
variants.impossible: A combination code can't render isn't drawn (Checkbox checked + indeterminate). List what's left in the contract's figma.variantCombinations.
variants.focusClip: In a variant that draws the focus ring (state=focus, and state=open where open shares the ring), every frame AROUND the ring layer has Clip Content OFF — the ring is a 3px spread shadow outside the control and a clipping parent cuts it — while the ring layer itself keeps Clip Content ON, because Figma only draws a shadow's spread on a clipping frame (owner's decision 2026-10-20). The Figma audit fails otherwise.
variants.propstar: The set sits in a Propstar table: rows = the main look axis, columns = the remaining axes grouped (invalid false/true × state, then disabled). Booleans are toggled in the panel, never expanded into columns. Regenerate the table (scripts/figma/propstar.js) in the same step every time a variant or property changes — labels written prop=value, checked by the audit (owner's rule 2026-10-21).

patterns.anatomy: legend (text + {prefix}-required) · options as instances of the item component · description · error — no state axis: hover/focus live in each item

props.title / description: TEXT, or BOOLEAN + TEXT {name}Text when optional
